prerequisites: Basic knowledge of calculus and statistics.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic principles of optimization and use optimization languages in a basic way.
Able to apply the basic principles of optimization to the field of mechanical engineering.
Able to apply simple regression and ANOVA to process data and draw conclusions.
Able to apply the fundamentals of queueing models to solve problems in the field of mechanical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to optimization and the use of optimization languages.
teaching_methods: Classroom presentations of concepts and problem-solving.
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on two partial exams (30% each), assignment submission and/or class participation (20%), and laboratory practices with a final report (20%). To pass, students must achieve a weighted grade of 5/10 or higher and submit all assessable activities; otherwise, the grade will be NP (not presented). Students who do not pass the course must take an ordinary resit exam covering all material. If still not passed, an extraordinary resit exam is available.
bibliography: Luiz Velho, Paulo Carvalho, Jonas Gomes, Luiz de Figueiredo Mathematical Optimization in Computer Graphics and Vision, 1st Edition - April 18, ISBN: 9780127159515
Mark Meerschaert ANOVA: Analysis of Variance Primer, 1994 ISBN: 0875813739
